analysis.title: Enterprise Products Partners LP (EPD): 3Q26 Recap: Constructive Message on Permian Gas Growth; Continue to Focus on Capital
key_insights: EPD 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA was $2,789m, 5% above GSe and 4% above consensus. Natural Gas volumes and optimization offset softer Crude contributions from lower optimization.

Little new color on the 2027 EBITDA outlook. GS believes investor expectations have been largely reset lower and sentiment improved slightly after the release. GS 2027 EBITDA estimate is $11,475m vs consensus $11,465m.

EPD raised its Permian gas outlook. 2030 wet gas production is now 38.6 bcf/d vs 35.4 bcf/d prior, closer to GSe of 40.1 bcf/d. Permian wet gas growth from 2025-2030 is now +9.9 bcf/d vs +6.7 bcf/d prior.

EPD now models Permian rich gas and NGLs growing 2.4x faster than crude, up from 1.6x. Management attributed the change to higher gas-to-oil ratios in wellhead production, not faster drilling. Barnett and Woodford formations reach 8-9x.
EPD projects an NGL 2030 exit rate of 5.2 mmb/d, up 0.5 mmb/d vs April expectations. GS notes stronger growth could imply better NGL recontracting rates and ability to fill pipes.

Management pointed to roughly 2 new Permian processing plants per year, vs 1-2 historically. GS adds two plants (2030/2032) and pulls one unannounced plant forward from 2030 to 2029, but does not underwrite the full two-per-year pace given market share competition.
Frac 15 is scheduled online in 2028. GS expects incremental fractionation capacity to be needed toward the end of the decade and post-2030.
Management talked down asset-level M&A because of high recent deal multiples. Leverage is now sub-3x. GS still sees M&A as more likely than significantly higher buybacks given EPD's history.

Capital allocation favors organic projects. Buybacks continue at a disciplined pace alongside the regular distribution. GS sees room to accelerate returns but expects higher organic capex to absorb near-term free cash flow growth.
GS raised its price target to $39 from $38 and stays Neutral. The target applies an unchanged 10.25x multiple to 2027 EBITDA. Price was $38.15 at the 30 Oct 2026 close, implying 2.2% upside.

market_movers.rationale: PT raised to $39 from $38 on higher EBITDA estimates and added Permian processing growth. Multiple unchanged at 10.25x 2027 EBITDA, with only 2.2% upside to the $38.15 price.

sector_views.rationale: Permian gas and NGL volume outlook is improving, but GS remains cautious on EPD's ability to capture incremental market share and on high-multiple M&A.

earnings_insights: EPD 3Q26 reported adjusted EBITDA $2,789m, +5% vs GSe and +4% vs consensus (reported quarter).
GSe FY26 adjusted EBITDA raised to $11,135m from $10,962m prior, vs consensus $11,033m (estimates).
GSe FY27 adjusted EBITDA raised to $11,475m from $11,403m prior, vs consensus $11,465m (estimates).
GSe 2028E adjusted EBITDA $12,181m vs prior $12,110m and consensus $12,012m (estimates).
Natural Gas beat on ongoing optimization (much smaller QoQ) plus stronger Permian and Haynesville volumes. Crude missed on lower optimization as 2Q26 SPR and demand-pull strength faded.

NGLs: Permian processing volumes drove fee-based margins, with modest beats in fractionation, transportation and export margin. Petrochemical & Refined Products gross margin also beat on seasonal refined products strength and completion of octane enhancement maintenance.
GS expects gas optimization contributions to step down further. Higher volumes across NGL, natural gas and petchem offset lower crude margin assumptions.
GS keeps about $3b of 2027 growth capex and $800M+ in annual unit buybacks in its model. Quarterly EPU estimates: 9/26 $0.75, 12/26E $0.79, 3/27E $0.78, 6/27E $0.79.
risk_factors: Upside risks: stronger NGL and petchem prices, FID of large capital projects with better than expected returns, and lower run-rate capex needs.
Downside risks: weaker recovery in NGL and petchem demand, more competition on NGL pipeline, frac and export, and high-multiple acquisitions.
Limited availability of large uncommitted producer acreage packages may constrain EPD's Permian market share gains.

tension_points.bull_case: Management's higher Permian gas and NGL outlook implies a bigger project backlog, about two processing plants per year, and better NGL recontracting rates and ability to fill pipes.
tension_points.bear_case: GS does not underwrite the full two-plant-per-year pace given competition for market share and limited uncommitted producer acreage packages. Higher organic capex could absorb near-term free cash flow.

theme_stances.key_argument: Higher gas-to-oil ratios raise Permian wet gas and NGL volumes, which supports EPD's project backlog and NGL recontracting.
theme_stances.evidence: gas growth expectations moved significantly higher and now closer to GSe
